requirements.statement: From the merge onward, /ship-build writes the run record (shipped.json) and custody anchor (custody.json) to refs/ensemble/records/<slug> through the records ref library, and writes nothing new under <git common dir>/ensemble/ship/.
requirements.source: TRD Objectives O1 (must pass: yes); roadmap item 4 brief; PM instruction 2026-11-12

requirements.statement: A ship run started before this change (records in the detached folder, nothing on the ref) still loads and resumes from that folder; the folder is read after the ref.
requirements.source: TRD Objectives O2 (must pass: yes); roadmap item 4 brief

requirements.statement: shipped.json on the ref carries work.branch and work.forge_feature_id (Forge's reader matches on them).
requirements.source: TRD Objectives O3 (must pass: no); roadmap item 4 brief; forge-vnext reader contract D5

requirements.statement: Custody's merge and deploy links resolve the anchor from the ref after the merge.
requirements.source: TRD Objectives O4 (must pass: yes); roadmap item 4 How it will be checked

requirements.statement: A plain /ship-build start (no --resume) on a fresh checkout or re-created worktree, with closed.json only on the records ref, anchors custody at the audited commit, not HEAD; with closed.json in neither place, an unclosed feature is still refused.
requirements.source: TRD Objectives O5 (must pass: yes); PM instruction 2026-11-12; deferred review finding

requirements.statement: ship-sequencer.js and custody.js keep sharing one path rule (ship-record-dir.js); neither takes the other's.
requirements.source: TRD Objectives O6 (must pass: no); roadmap item 4 brief

requirements.statement: After a merged record in a git repo, git cat-file -p refs/ensemble/records/<slug>:shipped.json shows the record, and no detached folder is created.
requirements.source: TRD Intended Change, How it will be checked (bullet 1)

requirements.statement: A fixture detached folder (record plus pointer, no ref) is loaded by status and continued by start --resume.
requirements.source: TRD Intended Change, How it will be checked

requirements.statement: custody check --link merge and --link deploy pass against the ref's anchor when the tracked custody.json disagrees.
requirements.source: TRD Intended Change, How it will be checked

requirements.statement: With the detached folder deleted and closed.json (audit.auditedCommit = X) only on the ref, a plain start anchors custody at X, not HEAD.
requirements.source: TRD Intended Change, How it will be checked

requirements.statement: A ref owned by another feature is never overwritten; a refused ref write is refused and the ref is unchanged.
requirements.source: TRD Intended Change, Decision (ref ownership rule); FIX-001 acceptance

requirements.statement: When the ref cannot be written, the record still lands in the detached folder (fallback).
requirements.source: TRD Intended Change, Decision; OQ-1 assumption

tasks.description: record-ref.js: add writeFiles({cwd, slug, files, identity, command, step, push}) committing files onto the ref tip with CAS, push when origin exists, refuse foreign-owned refs; export it.

ship-record-dir.js: shared path rule: refRun, writeRunRecord (ref first, detached fallback), readCustody/writeCustody, custodyPath naming <ref>:custody.json for ref-held runs; writePointer kept for reading only.

ship-sequencer.js: detach to the ref via writeRunRecord (no pointer); start stores work.forge_feature_id; loadState reads tracked, ref, then detached folder; start --resume fetches the ref; plain start restores and drops restored shipped.json; update header and test (d).
custody.js: readCustody/writeCustody through the shared rule; detach writes the anchor to the ref for ref-held runs; header comment.

ship-build.seam.test.js: new CLI-level cases for the full merge-detach run on the ref, plain start with folder deleted anchoring at audited commit, and read-record refusal when closed.json is nowhere.
Docs and vendoring: ship-build.md Step 1, Step 5 and readout; docs/guides/ship-build.md; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]; surface tests; copy changed libs and command to .claude/.

open_questions: OQ-1 (owner-only: no): Should a failed ref write fall back to the detached folder, or stop the run? Assumed: fall back and report it, because the merge already happened and the record must survive.
could_not_verify: Pushing the ref to GitHub and Forge's reader consuming the post-merge shipped.json: tests use a local bare origin, and the reader lives in forge-vnext.

record-ref.js write (the folder writer) run on a merged worktree would overwrite the ref's detached shipped.json with the stale tracked copy; 'Writers move to the ref' (roadmap item 3) must not call it after the detach. Not exercised here.
